Topics · The holy books together

What do the earlier books and the Quran share?

One God, one list of commands, one promise, side by side. Where could that single thread have come from?

Part 1 of 3

﴿وَٱعْبُدُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَلَا تُشْرِكُوا۟ بِهِۦ شَيْـًٔا ۖ وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَـٰنًا وَبِذِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَٱلْيَتَـٰمَىٰ وَٱلْمَسَـٰكِينِ وَٱلْجَارِ ذِى ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ وَٱلْجَارِ ٱلْجُنُبِ وَٱلصَّاحِبِ بِٱلْجَنۢبِ وَٱبْنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَمَا مَلَكَتْ أَيْمَـٰنُكُمْ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ مَن كَانَ مُخْتَالًا فَخُورًا﴾

Translation of the meaning

Worship Allāh and associate nothing with Him, and to parents do good, and to relatives, orphans, the needy, the near neighbor, the neighbor farther away, the companion at your side,[186] the traveler, and those whom your right hands possess. Indeed, Allāh does not like those who are self-deluding and boastful,

Translator's notes

[186] i.e., those whose acquaintance you have made. Also interpreted as the wife.

Quran · An-Nisa 4:36

Translation

“‘You shall not take vengeance, nor bear any grudge against the children of your people; but you shall love your neighbor as yourself. I am Yahweh. The stranger who lives as a foreigner with you shall be to you as the native-born among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am Yahweh your God.

Original · Hebrew

לֹֽא־תִקֹּ֤ם וְלֹֽא־תִטֹּר֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י עַמֶּ֔ךָ וְאָֽהַבְתָּ֥ לְרֵעֲךָ֖ כָּמ֑וֹךָ אֲנִ֖י יְהוָֽה׃ כְּאֶזְרָ֣ח מִכֶּם֩ יִהְיֶ֨ה לָכֶ֜ם הַגֵּ֣ר ׀ הַגָּ֣ר אִתְּכֶ֗ם וְאָהַבְתָּ֥ לוֹ֙ כָּמ֔וֹךָ כִּֽי־גֵרִ֥ים הֱיִיתֶ֖ם בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם אֲנִ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶֽם׃

the Torah (Leviticus) · 19:18, 34

World English Bible

Start with a list: worship God alone, and be good to parents and relatives, to orphans and the poor, to the neighbour near and the neighbour far, and to the traveller. Nothing in it is tied to one place or century. The Quran says a covenant in these same terms was taken long before from the Children of Israel, and it asks the same of its own readers. If two books make one request, what does that suggest about the one making it?

A question for you

Which item on that list do you find in your own tradition or conscience?

If you sayGod alone.
ThenThat is the first item on the list, and the first thing many books say.
If you sayGoodness to parents.
ThenIt comes straight after God alone, here and again in the next part. Notice that order.
If you sayThe orphan and the poor.
ThenThen you know what the prophets knew: faith shows in how those with no one behind them are treated.
If you sayAll of it.
ThenThen the question is larger than one item, and the next part sets a second list beside it.

Part 2 of 3

﴿قُلْ تَعَالَوْا۟ أَتْلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمْ عَلَيْكُمْ ۖ أَلَّا تُشْرِكُوا۟ بِهِۦ شَيْـًٔا ۖ وَبِٱلْوَٰلِدَيْنِ إِحْسَـٰنًا ۖ وَلَا تَقْتُلُوٓا۟ أَوْلَـٰدَكُم مِّنْ إِمْلَـٰقٍ ۖ نَّحْنُ نَرْزُقُكُمْ وَإِيَّاهُمْ ۖ وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا۟ ٱلْفَوَٰحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ ۖ وَلَا تَقْتُلُوا۟ ٱلنَّفْسَ ٱلَّتِى حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلْحَقِّ ۚ ذَٰلِكُمْ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَعْقِلُونَ١٥١ وَلَا تَقْرَبُوا۟ مَالَ ٱلْيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ ۖ وَأَوْفُوا۟ ٱلْكَيْلَ وَٱلْمِيزَانَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ ۖ لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا ۖ وَإِذَا قُلْتُمْ فَٱعْدِلُوا۟ وَلَوْ كَانَ ذَا قُرْبَىٰ ۖ وَبِعَهْدِ ٱللَّهِ أَوْفُوا۟ ۚ ذَٰلِكُمْ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَذَكَّرُونَ١٥٢﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you. [He commands] that you not associate anything with Him, and to parents, good treatment, and do not kill your children out of poverty; We will provide for you and them. And do not approach immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed. And do not kill the soul which Allāh has forbidden [to be killed] except by [legal] right. This has He instructed you that you may use reason." And do not approach the orphan's property except in a way that is best [i.e., intending improvement] until he reaches maturity. And give full measure and weight in justice. We do not charge any soul except [with that within] its capacity. And when you speak [i.e., testify], be just, even if [it concerns] a near relative. And the covenant of Allāh fulfill. This has He instructed you that you may remember.

Quran · Al-An'am 6:151-152

Translation

“You shall have just balances, a just ephah, and a just bath.

Original · Hebrew

מֹֽאזְנֵי־צֶ֧דֶק וְאֵֽיפַת־צֶ֛דֶק וּבַת־צֶ֖דֶק יְהִ֥י לָכֶֽם׃

Ezekiel · 45:10

World English Bible

The Quran has a second list, and it opens with an invitation: come, I will recite what your Lord has forbidden you. No partner with God. Goodness to parents. No killing of a child or of any soul. No indecency. Honest measure. Fair speech, even against your own kin. Keep your word. Set this beside the Ten Commandments and you will see the likeness yourself. Notice the form too. These are not general wisdom. Each is a command from God: do this, do not do that.

A question for you

What do you think explains two lists this close?

If you sayPeople everywhere reach the same morals.
ThenOften so, and conscience is part of the Quran's own account. Then ask why the one God stands at the head of each list.
If you sayOne took from the other.
ThenThat deserves careful weighing, and it has its own Step.
If you sayThey have one source.
ThenThen the question is what kind of source that could be. The next part comes closer.

Part 3 of 3

﴿وَلَقَدْ كَتَبْنَا فِى ٱلزَّبُورِ مِنۢ بَعْدِ ٱلذِّكْرِ أَنَّ ٱلْأَرْضَ يَرِثُهَا عِبَادِىَ ٱلصَّـٰلِحُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And We have already written in the book [of Psalms][909] after the [previous] mention[910] that the land [of Paradise] is inherited by My righteous servants.

Translator's notes

[909] Az-Zabūr can also mean "scriptures" in general. [910] i.e., the Torah. The "mention" may also refer to the original inscription with Allāh, i.e., the Preserved Slate (al-Lawḥ al-Maḥfūẓ).

Quran · Al-Anbiya 21:105

Translation

Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth.

μακάριοι οἱ πραεῖς, ὅτι αὐτοὶ κληρονομήσουσι τὴν γῆν.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 5:5

World English Bible

﴿أَمْ لَمْ يُنَبَّأْ بِمَا فِى صُحُفِ مُوسَىٰ٣٦ وَإِبْرَٰهِيمَ ٱلَّذِى وَفَّىٰٓ٣٧ أَلَّا تَزِرُ وَازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرَىٰ٣٨ وَأَن لَّيْسَ لِلْإِنسَـٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ٣٩﴾

Translation of the meaning

Or has he not been informed of what was in the scriptures of Moses And [of] Abraham, who fulfilled [his obligations] - That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another And that there is not for man except that [good] for which he strives

Quran · An-Najm 53:36-39

Translation

Also to you, Lord, belongs loving kindness, for you reward every man according to his work.

Original · Hebrew

וּלְךָֽ־אֲדֹנָ֥י חָ֑סֶד כִּֽי־אַתָּ֨ה תְשַׁלֵּ֖ם לְאִ֣ישׁ כְּֽמַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ׃

the Psalms · 62:12

World English Bible

Sometimes the Quran does more than resemble. It points. The verse says this was written in the Psalms: the earth will be inherited by God's righteous servants. You can open the Book of Psalms and find that promise there. A book that points to an older book, in words any reader can check, invites the comparison. Other verses list what stands in the scrolls of Moses and Abraham: no one carries another's load, and a person has only what they strove for.

A question for you

What does it do to a claim when a book names its source?

If you sayIt makes it testable.
ThenThat is what makes the agreement here something you can see for yourself, and not something you are told.
If you sayIt proves he took from it.
ThenThat is one possible reading. The Quran says its Prophet recited no book before it (29:48), so how the line reached him is a question of its own.
If you sayIt makes me want to read the Psalms.
ThenNothing better could come of it. The passage waits at the end of this Step.
